summary.text: Shontel Brown is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 11th Congressional District, which she has represented since winning a 2021 special election, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. A lifelong Clevelander and former marketing professional and small-business owner, she served on the Warrensville Heights city council and the Cuyahoga County Council and chaired the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party. In Congress she is vice ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee.

paragraphs.text: Brown was born in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1975, and her official biography describes her as a lifelong Clevelander who lives in Warrensville Heights.
She earned an associate degree in business management from Cuyahoga Community College and a bachelor's degree in organizational management from Wilberforce University.

Before her political career she owned Diversified Digital Solutions and worked as director of sales for Hotcards.com, a senior account manager with Radio One, and a marketing support representative with Telco Communications Group.

Brown entered public service in 2012 as a Warrensville Heights city council member, according to her official biography, and in 2014 she was elected to the Cuyahoga County Council to represent the 9th district, serving until 2021.
She was elected chair of the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party in 2017, becoming the first woman and first African American to hold the post.

She won the August 2021 Democratic primary and the November 2, 2021 special general election to succeed Marcia Fudge, who resigned to become Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, and was sworn in on November 4, 2021. She defeated former state Sen. Nina Turner in the 2022 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress, Brown serves on the House Agriculture Committee as vice ranking member, on the Oversight Committee as ranking member of its Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee, and on the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

She is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, the New Democrat Coalition and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, among other caucuses, and her official biography says she has authored bills on the racial health gap and anti-discrimination law.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 83.5% of the vote to Mike Kirchner's 16.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
